15 What is the centre of gravity of an object?
A
the geometrical centre of the object
B
the point at which the weight of the object may be considered to act
C
the point on the object about which there is a zero net torque
D
the point where gravity acts on the object

hints: Notice the wording in A about the geometrical centre and ask whether an irregular or non-uniform object would balance there.
Recall that weight is spread over the whole object, so the definition replaces this distributed weight by a single force $W$ at one point.
Compare C and D with that idea: C describes a torque balance condition and D suggests gravity acts only at one spot, rather than giving the standard weight model.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the textbook definition of centre of gravity, not a rule for finding it in a particular experiment.
Recall that every part of the object has weight, so for calculations the distributed weight is modelled as a single resultant force.
State the definition: the centre of gravity is the point at which the weight of the object may be considered to act.
Check the distractors: A is true only for uniform regular shapes, C confuses the definition with zero resultant moment about a pivot, and D wrongly implies gravity acts only at one point.
Matching the definition to the list gives the point where the weight may be considered to act. This is option B.

A.explanation: Incorrect. The geometrical centre equals the centre of gravity only for a uniform regular object, not for irregular or non-uniform objects.

B.explanation: Correct. The centre of gravity is defined as the single point where the whole weight $W$ can be taken to act for force and moment calculations.

C.explanation: Incorrect. Zero net torque depends on the pivot chosen and all applied forces, not the definition of the centre of gravity.

D.explanation: Incorrect. Gravity acts on every particle of mass in the object, not at one point only.
